cars.name: E30 M3
cars.trivia: The E30 M3 was built for Group A racing homologation and remains one of the most collectible M cars.

cars.name: E36 M3
cars.trivia: The E36 M3 broadened the M3 formula from a homologation special into a more usable performance coupe.

cars.name: E46 M3
cars.trivia: The E46 M3 CSL remains one of the most celebrated limited M cars of the 2000s.

cars.name: E39 M5
cars.trivia: The E39 M5 is often cited as a perfect balance of luxury sedan manners and raw V8 character.

cars.name: E60 M5
cars.trivia: The E60 M5's S85 V10 remains unique in M5 history — nothing before or after matched its cylinder count.

cars.name: E92 M3
cars.trivia: In the E9x family, E90 is sedan, E91 touring, E92 coupe, and E93 convertible — the M3 coupe is E92.

cars.name: F80 M3
cars.trivia: With the F80/F82 split, BMW separated M3 (sedan) and M4 (coupe/convertible) naming for the first time.

cars.name: G80 M3
cars.trivia: The G80 M3 Competition xDrive was the first all-wheel-drive M3 offered to customers.

cars.name: F87 M2 Competition
cars.trivia: The M2 Competition essentially dropped an M3/M4 engine into the smaller F87 package.

cars.name: G87 M2
cars.trivia: The G87 M2 continues BMW's tradition of a smaller, more focused M coupe below the M3/M4.

cars.name: E90 335i
cars.trivia: Pre-LCI E90 335i models used the twin-turbo N54 before the later N55 changeover.

cars.name: E90 335i
cars.trivia: LCI E90 335i cars switched from the twin-turbo N54 to the single twin-scroll N55.

cars.name: E82 135i
cars.trivia: The E82 135i gave enthusiasts a lighter, more playful alternative to the E90 335i with similar powertrain character.

cars.name: F30 340i
cars.trivia: The F30 340i helped make the B58 one of the most respected modern BMW sixes.

cars.name: G20 M340i
cars.trivia: The G20 M340i occupies the modern sweet spot between a regular 330i and a full M3.

cars.name: E60 535i
cars.trivia: E60 535i cars brought twin-turbo six-cylinder performance into the executive sedan class before the F10 era.

cars.name: F10 535i
cars.trivia: The F10 535i is a common real-world example of the N55 outside the 3 Series world.

cars.name: G30 540i
cars.trivia: The G30 540i continued BMW's pattern of packing strong turbo six performance into a refined executive package.

cars.name: E70 X5 35d
cars.trivia: The E70 xDrive35d brought serious diesel torque to North American X5 buyers and remains a favorite among diesel enthusiasts.

cars.name: E46 330i
cars.trivia: The E46 330i used the M54 naturally aspirated inline-six before the turbocharged E90 generation.

cars.name: E28 M5
cars.trivia: The E28 M5 was the first M5, hand-assembled in Munich and sold in the US only for 1987 and 1988.

cars.name: E24 M6
cars.trivia: The E24 M6 was the US version of the M635CSi, pairing the M1-derived S38 six with the sharknose 6 Series body.

cars.name: E90 M3
cars.trivia: The E90 M3 brought the M3 sedan back and was the first M3 powered by a V8, the 4.0-liter S65.

cars.name: E63 M6
cars.trivia: The E63 M6 shared the M5's S85 V10 and, unusually for a luxury coupe, could be ordered with a six-speed manual.

cars.name: F82 M4
cars.trivia: The F82 M4 was the first car to wear the M4 badge, splitting the M3 coupe into its own model line.

cars.name: G82 M4
cars.trivia: The G82 M4 introduced the tall vertical grille and, in CSL form, the most powerful six-cylinder ever put in an M car.

cars.name: F10 M5
cars.trivia: The F10 M5 traded the V10 for a twin-turbo S63 V8, and North America even got a six-speed manual option.

cars.name: F90 M5
cars.trivia: The F90 M5 was the first M5 with M xDrive all-wheel drive, which can switch to pure rear-wheel drive.

cars.name: G90 M5
cars.trivia: The G90 M5 is the first plug-in hybrid M5, pairing the S68 V8 with electric motors for 717 horsepower.

cars.name: F92 M8
cars.trivia: The F92 M8 made the 8 Series coupe BMW's V8 flagship and shares its S63 engine with the M5.

cars.name: E82 1M Coupe
cars.trivia: The 1M Coupe packed the N54 turbo six into the smaller 1 Series body, and only about 740 came to the US.

cars.name: G09 XM
cars.trivia: The XM is BMW M's first standalone model since the M1 and the first M car with a plug-in hybrid V8.

cars.name: F87 M2
cars.trivia: The original F87 M2 used the N55 single-turbo six before the M2 Competition arrived with the S55.

cars.name: E52 Z8
cars.trivia: The Z8 roadster borrowed the E39 M5's S62 V8 and is remembered as James Bond's car in The World Is Not Enough.

cars.name: E31 850i
cars.trivia: The E31 850i combined a 5.0-liter V12 with wedge-shaped 8 Series styling and was packed with 1990s tech.

cars.name: E38 740i
cars.trivia: The E38 740i paired the M62 V8 with restrained styling that many consider the high point of the 7 Series.

cars.name: E65 745i
cars.trivia: The E65 745i introduced the Bangle-era 7 Series look and the first iDrive, one of BMW's boldest redesigns.

cars.name: G01 X3 M40i
cars.trivia: The G01 X3 M40i brought the B58 six and M Performance tuning to BMW's best-selling SUV.

cars.name: G05 X5 40i
cars.trivia: The G05 X5 40i is the volume model of BMW's benchmark luxury SUV and runs the B58 inline-six.

cars.name: E53 X5 4.4i
cars.trivia: The E53 X5 was BMW's first SUV, and the 4.4i V8 version helped define the performance-luxury SUV segment.

cars.name: I01 i3
cars.trivia: The i3 was BMW's first mass-produced EV, built around a carbon-fiber structure and offered with a range extender.

cars.name: I12 i8
cars.trivia: The i8 paired a turbocharged three-cylinder with electric motors for supercar looks and sports-car efficiency.

cars.name: G26 i4 M50
cars.trivia: The i4 M50 was BMW M's first electric vehicle, with dual motors making it quicker than an M3.

cars.name: I20 iX xDrive50
cars.trivia: The iX serves as BMW's technology flagship EV, with dual-motor xDrive and a minimalist interior.

cars.name: G42 M240i
cars.trivia: The G42 M240i moved 2 Series Coupe production to Mexico and pairs the B58 inline-six with standard xDrive in the US.

cars.name: G42 230i
cars.trivia: The G42 230i is the rear-drive entry point to the 2 Series Coupe, running BMW's B48 turbo four.

cars.name: F22 M235i
cars.trivia: The F22 M235i brought M Performance power to the 2 Series Coupe before the M240i arrived with the B58.

cars.name: G22 M440i
cars.trivia: The G22 M440i brought the B58 and 48-volt mild hybrid assist to the 4 Series coupe with xDrive as standard in the US.

cars.name: F32 440i
cars.trivia: The F32 440i replaced the 435i's N55 with the B58, giving the 4 Series coupe one of BMW's most tunable sixes.

cars.name: F32 435i
cars.trivia: The F32 435i was the 4 Series coupe launch model, carrying the N55 turbo six from the E92 335i era.

cars.name: F30 335i
cars.trivia: The F30 335i carried the N55 into the sixth-generation 3 Series before the 340i and its B58 took over.

cars.name: F22 M240i
cars.trivia: The F22 M240i replaced the M235i and made the B58 inline-six the heart of BMW's compact coupe.

cars.name: G12 M760i xDrive
cars.trivia: The M760i xDrive was BMW's last V12 7 Series, using a 6.6-liter twin-turbo N74 and closing out the brand's V12 era.
